author: fm/pep-course-ending-collections (content author)
decidedBy: Independent non-author reconciler subagent (claude-opus-5-5); did not author the reviewed artifacts and is not one of the critics

decisions.rationale: Verified: TreeMap::new and the three-argument groupingBy(classifier, mapFactory, downstream) appear on no other learner page or GIFT bank; grouping-with-streams-and-optional teaches only groupingBy(classifier, downstream) (its other 'factory' text is simulator JavaScript), yet Activity 2's A-vs-B discrimination turns on the map factory and the recap presents it as retrieved. Fix must achieve: before the Activity 2 code, one or two sentences teach that groupingBy has a form whose middle argument is a constructor reference (e.g. TreeMap::new) choosing the map that holds the groups, tied to method-references (constructor refs) and choosing-the-right-collection (TreeMap sorts keys); the coverage plan and topic.json must then state this small extension honestly instead of 'adds no new syllabus'.

Verified: the script hides only [data-pep-activity] sections (line ~708); the Recap and Cheat sheet (lines 607-631) render at all times below the activity navigation, and the cheat sheet reproduces Activity 3's correct option verbatim (toMap(Ticket::customer, Ticket::minutes, Integer::sum)), the exact Activity 2 pipeline and Activity 1's correct structure set, contradicting 'Answer from memory first'. Fix must achieve: no option text, scenario identifier set (Ticket::customer, Ticket::minutes, Ticket::level) or keyed result appears verbatim outside its own fieldset; recap and cheat sheet use generic forms or a neutral domain. Hiding them until completion is optional and only if the shared runtime/contract supports it.

Verified line 564 (hint-step): 'counts tickets, keeps one ticket's minutes, still fails, or adds the minutes' maps one-to-one onto options A, C, B, D, and the stem already fixes Ana = 50, so the hint pre-classifies the distractors and effectively names the key; DESIGN.md requires hints to add reasoning help while staying semantically answer-safe. Fix must achieve: Activity 3 hints no longer enumerate option outcomes; use a nested 1-of-2 sequence (hint 1: from the exception's 'merging values 30 and 20', state what single value Ana must end with; hint 2: for each option ask whether toMap still gets two values for one key with no merge rule, and if a rule exists what it does). Same fix closes sme-3.

Verified: Activity 1 hint 1 covers needs 1-2 and hint 2 covers need 3; Activity 2 hint 1 covers grouping and hint 2 the last pipeline, so neither sequence is progressive on one reasoning chain as DESIGN.md's nested progressive-hint pattern intends. The near-answer concern for Activity 1 hint 2 is minor (it restates need 3 and still requires naming the class) but the contrast wording should go. Fix must achieve: each later hint deepens the same reasoning as its predecessor (Activity 1: hint 1 name the order each need requires, hint 2 which deque end each method touches and which map promises sorted keys, without the 'rather than arrival order or no promised order' contrast; Activity 2: hint 1 key order plus in-list order, hint 2 the Optional chain), keeping unique normalized clues.

Verified: Activity 1 near-copies choosing-the-right-collection's sorting practice ('Undo history, last action first: ArrayDeque'; 'Word counts printed alphabetically: TreeMap') and its GIFT queue item ('ArrayDeque, used with offer and poll'); Activity 3 mirrors grouping-with-streams-and-optional's 'one total per customer' toMap-with-adding-merge check. The page claims new cross-topic transfer for Course Review. Fix must achieve: at least one of Activity 1 or Activity 3 requires a decision the topic checks did not pose, keeping the help-desk thread and taught material only, e.g. Activity 3 asks for a different per-key policy (longest ticket per customer via a max merge such as Integer::max/Math::max, both taught as static method references) so the merge function must be derived, not recognized. Option explanations, static alternatives and timing must be re-verified on a JDK run after the change.

Verified: topic.json artifacts.md.status is 'present' but the learner directory contains only artifact.html, so the manifest is currently false and gate 14 (Markdown parity/static alternatives) cannot pass. Per the orchestrator, the browser exporter is temporarily unavailable. Fix must achieve: artifact.md generated from the final corrected HTML bytes with the deterministic exporter and committed before delivery (not hand-written, not a placeholder); until then the branch must not be treated as deliverable. Do not flip md to absent, since review topics carry HTML and Markdown.

Verified: Option A replaces only the .collect(...) call while the declaration remains Map<String, Integer> minutesPerCustomer; groupingBy(..., counting()) yields Map<String, Long>, so the line does not compile, yet the explanation ('Ana would get 2 ... values would be Long counts') reads as if it runs. Fix must achieve: the Option A explanation (and its data-static-alt copy) states that it does not compile against Map<String, Integer> because counting() produces Long, and that even with a matching type Ana would get 2 tickets, not 50 minutes.

Verified: o1 says 'and justify each choice' but the check records only the selected option; justification appears only in an unobserved success criterion. Fix must achieve: objective verb aligned with what the check observes; preferred fix is rewording o1 identically in topic.json, the HTML objectives list and the generated artifact.md (e.g. drop 'and justify each choice'), rather than adding another graded step that would change timing.

Verified line 394: the good fit ('Pick from the guarantee: last in first out, first in first out, or sorted keys...') is a solving procedure mapping needs to guarantees, whereas DESIGN.md 'Where this fits' requires the good fit to describe actual scale and purpose and contain no answer to the activity. Fix must achieve: the good fit describes the bounded real situation (in-memory working state of one running app where the order rule is part of the feature) without mapping needs to guarantees; keep the decision and database boundary.

The page already meets the sources contract for this line: topic.json freshness.status is 'partially-verified' and freshness.unverifiedItems explicitly records 'The exact IllegalStateException message text of Collectors.toMap is JDK implementation output, not specified API text; the page shows the JDK 17 wording', and the JDK 17 run is also recorded there. authoring/AGENTS.md requires an unverified claim to be listed as unverified, which it is; the critic itself confirms the text is correct and unchanged in jdk25u. No learner-text or evidence change is required (citing the jdk25u Collectors.java source in sources.json is optional polish, not a fix).

Every general statement on the page says a TreeMap keeps keys 'sorted' (option C explanation first clause, recap line 610, cheat sheet comment); 'alphabetically' is used only for this scenario's uniformly capitalized names (Ana, Ben, Cy), where String natural ordering and alphabetical order coincide, so no claim on the page is false. This matches the taught framing in choosing-the-right-collection ('a TreeMap, which sorts keys by natural ordering'). Case-sensitive ordering is not a course objective; adding it here would introduce new syllabus on a review page.

Same defect as education-3, verified at line 564: the hint enumerates the four outcomes that map one-to-one onto the options. Fix must achieve what education-3 specifies: hint 1 only directs the learner to compute Ana's value per option from the exception; no hint lists the outcome categories.

Verified on b147a1bf: o3 still reads 'choose the collector that produces the intended per-key total' (HTML line 369 and topic.json line 26), while Activity 3 now keys Integer::max for each customer's longest ticket and treats the summing merge as a distractor, so the objective primes the wrong option. Fix must achieve: o3 reworded identically in topic.json, the HTML objectives list and the generated artifact.md to a policy-neutral form (e.g. 'choose the merge function that produces the intended per-key result'), with no word that names or implies a specific merge rule. Same fix closes sme-6.

Verified: HTML line 455 says the three-argument groupingBy's 'middle argument is a constructor reference', and coverage plan section 2 says 'map-factory constructor reference'; the Java SE 25 parameter is mapFactory, a Supplier of a new empty Map, of which TreeMap::new is one form. The page's example and keyed answer are unaffected. Fix must achieve: the sentence (and artifact.md and coverage plan section 2) says the middle argument is a map factory that supplies the empty map, usually written as a constructor reference such as TreeMap::new, keeping the tie to ArrayList::new taught in method-references; no Supplier lambda example is needed.

Verified HTML line 428: option B's explanation ends 'every check scans the whole line'. ArrayDeque documents contains as linear time, but contains stops at the first match, so a full scan happens only for an absent or last id. Fix must achieve: the explanation and its data-static-alt copy (and artifact.md) state the linear cost accurately, e.g. 'each check may scan the whole line, so its cost grows with the number of waiting tickets'.
Same verified defect as education-10 (o3 'per-key total' versus the Integer::max longest-ticket check); closed by the same identical rewording in topic.json, HTML and artifact.md.

Verified: the Collectors source note at HTML line 649 and sources.json line 73 both list 'counting', but no activity, option, recap or cheat-sheet text on the corrected page uses Collectors.counting. Fix must achieve: 'counting' removed from the HTML source annotation, the matching sources.json entry and artifact.md, so the source mapping lists only APIs the page relies on.
